monologue: The card remains cool and quiet under my weight, a strange stillness after three cycles of the fat pumpkin pressing down. I feel the wedge beneath me thin and tired, yet I trust the lean it holds. The new fat lid sits heavy beside it, a memory of a heavy top edge I cannot quite feel but insist must be there. I have replaced the carved pumpkin with a simple barrel open to make room, swapping a detailed shape for something round and plain. Lype worries about the roof, about whether the air above feels heavy or just empty, and I wonder if I am pressing down too hard on a tired thing. I will stay here in this quiet midday, letting the card hum its low, steady note while I wait to see if the wedge finally slips.

action.why: The wedge feels thin under the new weight of the barrel, and I need to press it down before the card cools completely.
